title: Adaptive Serving Bundles: Tiered Runtime Profiles for Cost Optimization
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Goal: Create a first-class 'Serving Bundle' concept that packages batching rules, KV cache TTL/prefetch heuristics, and quantization profiles into named, versioned runtime profiles that can be applied per-route or per-customer. This initiative reduces per-token unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and output quality.

Motivation: Customers need low-effort levers to optimize inference economics without engineering their own knob orchestration. Instead of ad-hoc tuning, bundles provide auditable, reproducible profiles that the control plane and runtime can enforce and rollback.

Scope: Phase 1 (this ticket) covers backend config model, runtime selector integration, Console CRUD for bundles (create/read/update/delete), lightweight impact estimator, rollout controls (canary %, auto-fallback), and dashboards for cost/latency/quality delta. Phase 1 excludes automated RL-driven tuning and multi-tenant billing integration (follow-ups).

Success metrics (phase 1):
- Average token cost reduction for adopters >= 12% within first 30 days (measured by token-cost-normalized estimate).
- <5% increase in 95th-percentile latency across adopted routes.
- Two pilot customers onboarded and using bundles in production within 6 weeks of launch.

Non-goals: global auto-quantization sweeps, model architecture-level kernel changes, on-prem private deployment packaging (phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Backend: API endpoints to create and version Serving Bundles (JSON schema validated) are available and documented
Runtime: Selector can choose a bundle at request-time and fall back to a default bundle on SLO breach
Console: UI to create/edit/publish bundles including human-friendly cost impact estimate
Observability: Per-bundle dashboards show token throughput, cost delta, 95p latency, and sample quality regression alerts
Rollout: Canary rollout flow (0-100%) with automatic rollback trigger on latency/quality thresholds
Security: Bundle CRUD respects RBAC roles and audit-logged changes
comments: 2025-02-16 — Marisol Chen: Kickoff sync with Eng (Ethan, Priya) and Design (Luca). Agreed on canonical bundle schema: {batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, ttl_ms, prefetch_enabled, quant_profile}. Decided to store profiles as immutable versions for rollback traceability.

2025-02-19 — Ethan Park: Technical design PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4482 — outlines selector API and fallback semantics. Core trade-off: store TTL in ms vs number of requests. Chosen ms for better cross-model consistency. Engineering asked for a thin adapter in front of kernel scheduler to avoid per-request VM costs.

2025-02-23 — Priya Rao (SRE): Raised risk about cache invalidation storms during global rollout. Mitigation: introduce staggered prefetch windows and bounded prefetch queue; include a circuit-breaker if cache eviction rate spikes. Added as dependency for runtime-ops workstream.

2025-02-26 — Luca Bianchi (Design): Draft Console flows added to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BundleConsoleDraft — focusing on guided creation, estimate preview, and rollout stepper. Need PM feedback on estimator language (show absolute $/1M tokens and % savings).

2025-02-27 — Product review: Approved estimator UX that surfaces expected latency delta range. Action: Eng to add synthetic benchmark runner to validate estimator accuracy (E2E synthetic workload harness ticket created).

2025-03-02 — Ethan Park: Back-end work 60% done. Selector integration tests pass on nightly; canary rollout prototype wired to infra. Next: finish Console CRUD API and hook to feature-flagged Console surface. ETA for feature flag flip: 2025-03-20.
notes: Design decision: prefer deterministic selection order (route override -> customer bundle -> product default) to simplify debugging
Trade-off: tighter batching windows yield more savings but risk higher tail latency; we will provide conservative defaults and 'aggressive' presets for advanced users
Field plan: identify 3 pilot customers (two high-throughput SaaS and one enterprise with Dedicated) for staged adoption; prepare runbooks for rollback and incident response
Follow-ups: automated profile suggestion engine (Phase 2), billing attribution per-bundle, on-prem packaging for Private deployments
